fieldMarks: Short 'bobbed' tail about 10-18 cm (4-7 in), black on top at the tip and white underneath.
Buff to brown or grey coat with dark spots and streaks; white belly often with black spots.
Short ear tufts, backs of the ears black, and ruffs of hair on the sides of the head.
65-105 cm long; adult females about 9-11 kg and males about 14 kg (20-25 lb and 30 lb in Minnesota).
Smaller, less furry feet and a flatter back than the Canada lynx.
behavior: Solitary; sexes interact almost only in the breeding season.
Mostly nocturnal and crepuscular; terrestrial but a good climber.
Strictly carnivorous stalk-and-pounce hunter of mice, hares, squirrels, birds and deer fawns; can kill adult deer.
Marks territory with scent and yowls during the breeding season.
habitat: Forests, semi-desert, mountains and brushland; in Minnesota favours prey-rich young aspen forest and cedar swamps. Dens in hollow trees, thickets, brush piles or rocky areas.
range: Throughout North America from southern Canada to southern Mexico, with the highest U.S. densities in the Southeast.

lookalikes.name: Canada lynx
lookalikes.howToTell: The lynx has long ear tufts, huge snowshoe-like feet, a raised hind end, and a tail tip that is black all the way around.
